activity_context.topic_title: Properties of Line Integrals of Vector-Valued Functions

feedback.problem: Let $F(x,y)=(x-3y)\,i+2\,j$ and let $C$ be the path defined by $r(t)=⟨t,\,{t}^{2}+1⟩$ for $t\in [0,1].$ Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r?$
feedback.worked_solution:
Given a piecewise-smooth path $C$ and a vector field 

$$
F(x,y)=P(x,y)\,i+Q(x,y)\,j
$$

defined on $C,$ we have

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{C}P(x,y)\,\text{d}x+Q(x,y)\,\text{d}y.
$$

Therefore, in our case, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{C}(x-3y)\,\text{d}x+2\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
